summary.value: The Barbu de Watermael is a Belgian bantam and one of the smallest chickens kept anywhere. Antoine Dresse developed it early in the 1900s on an estate at Watermael-Boitsfort, near Brussels, and it was first exhibited in 1922. He never said which breeds he used, though the Barbu d'Anvers was certainly one of them. The Watermael looks much like the d'Anvers but is smaller and carries a narrow crest swept back over the head, a three part beard and muff, and a rose comb ending in three little points. Cocks weigh about 1.3 to 1.5 pounds and hens 1 to 1.2 pounds. Belgium accepts more than thirty colors, and in the United States it is known as the Watermaal, shown in black, blue, buff, mottled, quail and white. It is kept almost only as an ornamental and show bird and is considered in danger in its home country.
